pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORIES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you predict the outcome of a story even before you read it?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words
2. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORIES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORIES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words

What this means
In this part you learn to use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Answer direct and inferential questions from a short story

What this means
In this part you learn to answer direct and inferential questions from a short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer direct and inferential questions from a short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer direct and inferential questions from a short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories to a partner. (skill: answer direct and inferential questions from a short story)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words.
3. Practise this skill: answer direct and inferential questions from a short story.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you predict the outcome of a story even before you read it?
2. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words in a story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words.
5. Be able to: answer direct and inferential questions from a short story.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
